title: a record-triggered flow that a parent also starts as a subflow is judged as if record were its trigger row: the value-envelope date-text refusal reads the parent's record with the child's field types
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQAXHSQEgnYyx9tstb

Filing gate: ① measured scope (the stand-down predicate in PR #34654, residue 2 of its dev report). ⛔ Not a claim.

Blocked-by: #34451
Suggested-grade: p2 · domain:server — a false refusal at `registerFlow` is fatal (the flow does not register), the same door #34451 makes refusing.

## What

PR #34654 (#34451) types a flow value envelope for the date-text verdicts only where the run's `record` is the typed object's row: a record-triggered start (`deriveTriggerBinding` record_change; lint `faultOutcomeOf`) or a time-relative sweep of the typed object, with no `record` variable of the flow's own. The predicate reads the flow's own start node. A flow whose start is record-triggered can ALSO be started by a parent through a `subflow` (or `map`) node, and on that entrance `record` is the record the parent hands down, not a row of the child's trigger object. Both doors still judge `record.<field>` with the child's field types, so a child envelope written for the parent's record (`timestamp(record.<field>)` where the parent's field is a `datetime` and the child object's same-named field is a `date`) is refused although it evaluates.

## Where (after #34654)

- `packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts`: `runBindsTypedRow` reads the flow's own start only.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`: the envelope typing follows `faultOutcomeOf` for the flow alone; lint already reads entrances across the stack (`flowCelEntrances`), the engine registers one flow at a time.

## Done when

An envelope in a flow that some entrance starts with a record other than its trigger row is not refused on the trigger object's field types (lint, with the stack's entrances in hand), and the engine either reaches the same answer or states in its docblock why it cannot see the entrance; a CONTROL keeps the plain record-triggered flow refused.

Related: #34451, #34662 (same verdict family).

Dedupe words: subflow entrance record parent row value envelope, runBindsTypedRow record-triggered child flow, faultOutcomeOf entrance.
